newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MANCHESTER UNITED PAY-PER-VIEW TRIAL POSSIBLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MANCHESTER UNITED PAY-PER-VIEW TRIAL POSSIBLE.

text.p: Manchester United may become the first British soccer club chosen for pay-per-view satellite television.
United could be used in a trial before the end of the season, chief executive Martin Edwards told the club's annual meeting on Friday.
The premier league and Rupert Murdoch's BSkyB organisation have given themselves two years to work out a structure for the controversial pay-as-you-watch system.
Edwards also defended Manchester United's position over the issuing of new strips on a regular basis.
"Liverpool have had far more shirts that we have had because they keep changing their sponsors. Every football club has three strips nowadays and they change them on a two-year cycle."
Shareholders were also told to end speculation about a takeover of the club.

"We are mindful of the position of Manchester United and we are also aware that we are a public company but I don't want people to continue talking about takeovers because it only gives people ideas," said company chairman Sir Roland Smith.
"I can't guarantee anything, of course, but we won't do anything to encourage anything along those lines."

The club made profits of 15.4 million pounds ($25.9 million) compared with 20 million pounds ($33.6 million) the previous year. It said this was largely the result of the rebuilding of the North Stand.

On a lighter note, suggestions that singing areas be brought back for fans were rejected because it would be too difficult to change arrangements involving the 40,000 season ticket holders who attend each home game.
